PON Definition: A program whose beneficiaries demonstrated one or more of the following results within the past year: -Ensure prompt, timely payment of interest to all holders of U.S. public debt.

PON2: Strengthen Operational Readiness of Defense Units
PON Definition: A program whose beneficiaries demonstrated one or more of the following results within the past year: -Conducted unit-level exercises or simulations to validate readiness for joint or strategic defense missions; -Met operational benchmarks in force structure, equipment readiness, and logistical support for rapid deployment; -Demonstrated coordinated capability to execute assigned missions in domestic or international security contexts.

A program whose beneficiaries attained one or more of the following results within the past year: -Conducted maintenance, repair, or servicing activities to ensure operational availability or modernization of military equipment and vehicles; -Maintained or improved infrastructure essential to military operations, including facilities; -Ensured provisioning of necessary materials and equipment to support ongoing missions and training.

A program whose beneficiaries demonstrated one or more of the following results within the past year: -Improved internal business solutions (e.g., automation of operational processes, adoption of new technology, etc.); -Improved ability to adjust operations to meet market demands (e.g., development of new or improved services or products, improved marketing, etc.); -Improved ability to withstand unforeseen shocks and external economic events (e.g., financial plan to enable future organizational functioning and growth, sufficient savings, etc.).

A program whose beneficiaries demonstrated one or more of the following results within the past year:  -Increased sales, revenue, profits, or production; -Expansion of client base or access to new markets; -Increased number of employees.

A program whose beneficiaries demonstrated one or more of the following results within the past year: -Sufficient capacity to prevent and treat diseases (i.e., organizational structures, highly trained workforces, and cross-agency partnerships); -Establishment of a leadership and governance structure to allocate public health resources; -Development of the capabilities for emergency risk management.

A program whose beneficiaries attained one or more of the following results within the past year: -Placement in a permanent home through adoption or reunification; -Stayed in a permanent home that they were previously placed in through adoption or reunification.

A program whose beneficiaries demonstrated one or more of the following results within the past year: -Provision of safe and effective healthcare; -Provision of healthcare that fosters respectful treatment, open communication between patients and physicians, alignment between patient preferences and treatments received, and higher levels of patient satisfaction; -Provision of time-and cost-efficient healthcare.

A program whose beneficiaries demonstrated one or more of the following results within the past year: -Reduced exposure to environmental and community risk factors associated with illness or disease; -Positive behavior changes that reduce risk of chronic diseases (e.g., maintaining a nutritious diet, avoiding tobacco and excessive drinking, getting regular health screenings, being physically active); -Improved physical health indicators linked to  disease prevention (e.g., better respiratory function, improved sleep).

A program whose beneficiaries have gained access to one or more of the following results within the past year: -Safe, quality housing (rented or owned) that meets personal needs and is free or affordable; -Safe housing includes being asbestos free, lead free, and structurally sound; -Free or affordable includes subsidized housing and/or other forms of rent assistance.

A program whose beneficiaries achieved one or more of the following results within the past year: -Received a tax credit, deduction, or exemption based on eligibility tied to income, caregiving, education, or other socially valuable activity; -Benefited from expanded access to refundable or nonrefundable credits aimed at reducing inequality (e.g., EITC, Child Tax Credit); -Increased after-tax income as a result of policy measures intended to promote fairness in the tax system.
